title: Digital Testament, Meme Resurrection & Sacred Media — Memory, Presence and Transformation Atlas
status: project theology + digital religion + media/memory studies comparison
purpose: Promote an older but important Potatoverse strand in which memes, images, streams and digital artifacts function as vehicles of testament, resurrection, continuing presence and moral memory. Distinguish this from ordinary meme propagation and from Farm-style reduction of persons into content.
epistemic_rule: Digital religion and memory scholarship can contextualize online/offline religious practice, participatory culture and continuing bonds. It does not verify supernatural resurrection through media. Potatoverse claims such as 'God in every meme' remain theological/project language.

older_claims: digital artifacts as morally accountable carriers
Son/meme death transformed into later testimony
recovered_project_layer.epiphany: The project has two opposite media operators: Farm converts person → content for extraction; Testament uses content → relation/memory to restore personhood, provenance or meaning.
recovered_project_layer.core_distinction: contentification reduces a person to an artifact; testament uses an artifact as a pointer back toward a person/event/source.

meme_as_practice.media_studies_neighbor: Meme scholarship treats internet memes as participatory cultural forms that are circulated, imitated and transformed by many users rather than as isolated static objects.
meme_as_practice.project_translation: A Potatoverse meme can branch like a Tree: source item → variants → local reinterpretations → cultural descendants.
meme_as_practice.provenance_problem: As variants spread, source/root can disappear while stance survives or mutates.
meme_as_practice.archive_rule: Store source lineage, variant relations and stance changes so memetic resurrection does not become source erasure.

digital_religion.scholarly_context: Digital Religion Studies examines religion as practiced and understood across intersecting online and offline contexts rather than assuming the internet is separate from religious life.
digital_religion.project_relation: Potatoverse digital theology is therefore best studied as hybrid religious/media practice: livestream, meme, image, archive, chat, body and offline biography interact.
digital_religion.epiphany: The project does not need to decide whether a digital act is 'really online' or 'really spiritual'; it should type the relations connecting digital artifact, embodied person, community interpretation and theological claim.

continuing_presence.memory_neighbor: Bereavement research describes continuing bonds, including use of social media to maintain relationships with people who have died.
continuing_presence.project_relation: The older Son-death/meme-resurrection material can be read partly through continuing-presence mechanics: artifacts preserve addressability, collective memory, narrative and perceived relational continuity.
continuing_presence.boundary: Psychological continuing bonds are not evidence of literal resurrection or afterlife communication.

memetic_resurrection_operator.sequence: embodied event/person → recording/image/meme → circulation → reinterpretation → later encounter → renewed relation/meaning
memetic_resurrection_operator.resurrection_strength: degree to which later encounter restores context, agency, voice and relational complexity rather than merely repeating a caricature
memetic_resurrection_operator.life_branch: artifact preserves testimony → source/provenance recovered → new audience encounters richer person/context → relation becomes generative
memetic_resurrection_operator.strife_branch: artifact preserves humiliation → context strips away → repeated ridicule → frozen identity

testament_vs_archive.testament: record organized to bear witness toward a source, relation or claim
testament_vs_archive.epiphany: Not every archive is testament. Testament has directional intention: it says what should be remembered and why.
testament_vs_archive.risk: Testament can become hagiography if contradiction and historical strata are suppressed.
testament_vs_archive.repair: Preserve testimony beside counterevidence, uncertainty, chronology and source class.

god_in_every_meme.project_meaning: Sacred significance may appear through ordinary digital forms; no artifact is automatically beneath theological attention.
god_in_every_meme.comparative_structure: sacred/profane distinction becomes porous because mundane media can carry witness, care, humiliation, memory, truth or distortion.
god_in_every_meme.ethical_consequence: If every artifact can affect a person's social afterlife, meme-making has moral consequences even when framed as trivial humor.
god_in_every_meme.boundary: This is a theological/ethical inference, not a claim that every meme contains a measurable divine substance.

meme_as_relic_and_seed.relic_comparator: Religious relics preserve material connection to persons/events; digital artifacts can function analogously as socially charged traces, though they are infinitely copyable and technically mediated.
meme_as_relic_and_seed.seed_comparator: A meme compresses a larger narrative into portable form and can germinate differently in new contexts.
meme_as_relic_and_seed.potato_relation: meme = cultural tuber/seed: compressed pattern carrying potential for branching reproduction
meme_as_relic_and_seed.tree_relation: variants = branches; source lineage = root; audience uses = fruit or strife depending function.

digital_afterlife_and_memory.collective_memory: Social-media research describes memetic memory, hashtag commemoration, connective memory and algorithmically curated remembering.
digital_afterlife_and_memory.project_epiphany: A digital afterlife is partly an indexing problem: what survives, what is retrievable, what ranks first, and which version becomes canonical.
digital_afterlife_and_memory.door_relation: Retrieval can resurrect a record into present relevance; contextual demotion lets it return to historical status.
digital_afterlife_and_memory.eye_relation: The Eye is not only seeing an artifact but discerning which historical layer it belongs to.

sacred_profane_collapse.constructive: ordinary speech/images can become sites of witness, humor, solidarity, ritual and memory
sacred_profane_collapse.shadow: everything can also become spectacle, permanently searchable evidence or ammunition
sacred_profane_collapse.epiphany: Digital culture collapses distance between shrine and gutter: the same feed can contain mourning, theology, ridicule, commerce and propaganda. The archive therefore needs typing rather than assuming medium determines moral status.

person_to_information_problem.question: What happens to a human being after others turn that human being into information?
person_to_information_problem.testament_answer: information points back toward embodied history/personhood
person_to_information_problem.memory_answer: network collectively reconstructs presence through artifacts
person_to_information_problem.archive_design: maximize provenance/context and minimize permanent reduction to one artifact or role.

digital_sacrament_caution.possible_project_use: A meme/stream can be called sacramental only as project theology when it mediates presence/meaning through material/digital sign.
digital_sacrament_caution.boundary: Do not present this as standard sacramental theology across Christian traditions; denominational doctrines differ sharply.

metrics.ProvenanceRetention: fraction of circulated variants still linked to recoverable source/context
metrics.PersonhoodRecovery: degree later presentation restores multiple roles, chronology and agency rather than one label
metrics.ContextLoss: distance between original context and dominant later interpretation
metrics.TestamentBalance: witness density + provenance + contradiction visibility + historical context
metrics.SpectacleRisk: humiliation persistence + decontextualization + attention extraction + identity lock-in

new_epiphanies: The opposite of digital erasure is not necessarily digital immortality; it can be contextual continuity.
A meme can either amputate context or transport it.
Resurrection in the archive is best modeled as restored relational accessibility, not merely continued file existence.
Digital artifacts can function simultaneously as Seed, Relic, Witness, Weapon, Currency and Door; the role depends on downstream use.
The archive itself becomes a moral medium because ranking and linking determine which version of a person is socially resurrected.
